source_caption:
Roommates follows a group of young adults who end up sharing the same home while trying to figure out their careers, relationships, friendships, and personal lives. What seems like a simple living arrangement quickly becomes complicated when their different personalities and lifestyles begin to collide.
Living under one roof means dealing with disagreements, unexpected situations, relationship drama, and responsibilities that affect everyone. At the same time, the roommates gradually develop friendships and connections that make the house feel more like a family.
As each character faces their own struggles, they learn that independence does not mean handling everything alone. Their experiences force them to communicate, compromise, and sometimes choose between what they want and what is best for the people around them.
The story explores themes of friendship, love, trust, independence, responsibility, and growing up. Every roommate brings a different perspective, creating both conflict and moments of genuine connection.
What makes Roommates compelling is how ordinary situations can quickly turn into unexpected drama when several different lives are sharing the same space.
More than just a story about people living together, Roommates is about the relationships formed when strangers become part of each other's everyday lives.
💬 Could you survive living with people who have completely different personalities from you?

source_details.synopsis: Roommates is a 1995 American comedy-drama film, starring Peter Falk, D. B. Sweeney, and Julianne Moore, directed by Peter Yates. The original music score was composed by Elmer Bernstein. The film was marketed with the tagline, "Some people talk. Some people listen. When you're 107 and going strong, you do whatever you want."
